title: #1. Hobby / Archery
text:
When I have free time, I enjoy doing archery.

I actually set up my own shooting area on my land, so I practice every Saturday.

A few years ago, I watched the Olympic Games and was really impressed by the Korean archery team. That moment sparked my curiosity, so I decided to try it myself.

At first, my accuracy was terrible, especially outdoors. But the more I practiced, the easier it became to hit the target.

What I find most valuable about archery is the focus it requires. In fact, I have noticed that this carries over into my work as a programmer. I can concentrate on problems more clearly and stay locked in for longer.

That is why archery is not just a hobby for me; it actively makes me better at what I do.

title: #2. Social Media
text:
Social media has both clear benefits and real downsides.

On the positive side, it is much easier to reconnect with people from your past. For example, I am actually trying to find a Chinese friend that I studied with at university. Without social media, that would be almost impossible.

But there are real downsides too. One big problem is safety. Even if your account is set to private, someone can create a fake profile, act friendly, and get full access once you follow them back. That is pretty hard to prevent.

The other issue is more personal. I just want to relax quietly, play games, or watch short videos without being bombarded by news or other people's posts. Social media makes that really hard.

So yes, it is useful for staying connected, but it also makes it harder to stay private and harder to just switch off.

title: #3. Technology / AI
text:
Technology, especially AI, has changed our lives in a pretty dramatic way.

On the positive side, it has made a lot of tasks much faster and easier. As a programmer, I use AI tools almost every day for writing code, fixing bugs, and looking things up. What used to take hours can now take minutes.

But honestly, that is also what worries me. AI is getting good enough to replace a lot of software jobs, which is part of why I am planning to shift my career toward electrical engineering. Physical, hands-on work is a lot harder for AI to replace.

Another problem is that people may depend on AI too much. If people always let AI think for them, they may lose their own problem-solving skills. So, I think AI is very useful, but we have to be careful when we use AI.

title: #4. Environment
text:
In my opinion, protecting the environment is important, but I think individual actions have limited impact.

Climate change is clearly a real problem. Temperatures are rising and extreme weather is becoming more common. Also, most of this is caused by human activity.

However, I think the real responsibility is on large companies and governments. A large company can create much more pollution than one person. So I think it is unfair to blame only individuals.

That said, I still think individuals should do something. Small habits like saving electricity or buying less can still help. Also, if enough people change their behaviour, it puts pressure on companies to change too.

So in my opinion, protecting the environment matters. But real change has to come from companies and governments.

title: #5. Historical Place in Korea
text:
One historical place that I think is worth mentioning is Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon, South Korea.

It was built in the late 18th Century by King Jeongjo. It was not only built for military defense, but also a symbol of his political vision and his love for his father.

Also, it's a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and I think it deserves that recognition. The walls and gates are still standing, and you can actually walk along them and see the whole city from above.

I actually live near Suwon, so I have been there a few times. To me, it doesn't feel like a typical museum. It feels like a real historical place.

So if someone asked me to recommend a historical place in Korea, Hwaseong Fortress would be my first answer.

title: #6. Money and Happiness
text:
In my opinion, managing personal finances is important because money and happiness are closely related, but not directly.

Most people earn their income from work, so they should spend it carefully on essential expenses first.

In my case, I try to spend money on important things, such as food, transportation, education, and health, and I usually invest spare money in stocks.

Money doesn't buy happiness by itself. However, it removes a lot of stress, especially when people are worried about rent, bills, education, or health.

For me personally, I feel most comfortable when I have enough financial stability to make my own choices. That sense of control is more important than the actual amount.

Also, I think health and money are connected. Staying healthy saves money in the long run. And having enough money makes it easier to take care of your health.

In my opinion, money is not the key to happiness.

title: #7. Chuseok
text:
One tradition that is very important in Korea is Chuseok, which is basically the Korean harvest festival.

It is not only a family holiday, but also a cultural tradition that brings people together.

During this time, many Koreans travel back to their hometown to spend time with their family.

Families also prepare traditional food, especially songpyeon, which is a type of rice cake.

To me, these activities are meaningful because they connect family, culture, and community.

Chuseok also helps people stay connected to their roots, even in modern life.

I think this is important because many people are busy these days and do not have many chances to think about their traditions.

So, I believe Chuseok is not just a holiday. It is a tradition that shows Korean culture, family values, and a sense of community.

title: #8. Qualities for Success
text:
I think three qualities are important for success: curiosity, adaptability, and persistence.

First, curiosity helps people keep learning. For example, I started archery and programming because I found them interesting. When I am curious, I can learn without being forced.

Second, adaptability is important because the world changes fast. I worked as a programmer, but when I saw AI changing the industry, I decided to change my direction. It was not easy, but I think flexible people have more chances.

Finally, persistence matters. When I started archery, I could not hit the target well. When I started programming, I was also confused. But the more I practiced, the easier it became.

So, I believe success is not only about talent. It is about staying curious, adapting to change, and not giving up.

title: #9. Indie Game Studio
text:
If I had a chance to start my own business, I would build a small game company.

For me, this would not be just about making money. It would be connected to my background, my interests, and my long-term goals.

Since I have experience in game development, I understand that making a good game requires planning, teamwork, and steady improvement.

I would not try to build a huge company at first. Instead, I would start with a small team and focus on one polished project.

Of course, this kind of business could be risky because it requires funding, management skills, and patience.

However, I believe a small game company could give talented developers a chance to bring their ideas to life.

If the company grows slowly and sustainably, it could become both meaningful and profitable.

So, if I had this kind of chance, I would use it to build a business that fits my experience and future goals.

title: #10. Birthday Script
text:
In Korea, birthdays are usually celebrated with family or close friends.

One common tradition is eating seaweed soup. It has a special meaning because mothers often eat it after giving birth. So eating it on a birthday is a way to remember and appreciate your mother.

Also, people prepare tteok, which is a Korean rice cake, instead of a regular birthday cake. It can make the birthday feel more traditional.

Personally, I prefer a quiet birthday with family or close friends. I do not need a big party. A simple meal, a short conversation, and a sincere message are enough for me.

What makes a birthday meaningful is not the food or gifts, but the feeling that people remember you and care about you.

So, I think birthdays are not only about gifts or parties. They are about spending time with people who remember you.

title: #11. Art & Creativity
text:
I think art is not limited to drawing or painting.

As a game developer, I often think about art as a way to communicate ideas and emotions to an audience.

A game, like a painting or a film, can be a creative medium. It has a visual style, a mood, and a message.

I didn't think of myself as an artistic person when I was younger. But over time, I realized that creativity is not only about making something beautiful.

It is about expressing an idea in a way that other people can feel and understand.

So, I believe art and creativity are closely connected to how people communicate and express themselves, regardless of the medium.

title: #12. Person I Admire
text:
One person I truly admire is Hidetaka Miyazaki.

He is a game director, best known for creating Dark Souls and Elden Ring.

When he was young, he had poor eyesight and could not read books easily. So his mother used to read fantasy novels to him, and he had to imagine the world in his own head.

I think this shaped how he makes games. His games do not explain things directly. Players have to explore and imagine the story themselves, just like he did as a child.

What I admire most is that he turned a difficulty into something unique, instead of seeing it only as a limitation.

To me, he is inspiring because he used his weakness as a source of creativity.

title: #13. Favorite Book / Movie
text:
One story that had a big impact on me is The Last of Us.

It is originally a game, but the story is so strong that it feels like a novel or a film.

The story happens after a pandemic. A man named Joel has to protect a young girl named Ellie and bring her to a safe place. But the journey becomes more than that.

What makes it special is not the action. It is the relationship between them.

They start as strangers, but slowly they begin to trust and care for each other like family.

I think this story stays with me because it feels emotionally honest. It doesn't have a simple happy ending, and it asks hard questions about love, sacrifice, and survival.

That is why I remember this story. It shows that a good story can be powerful even when it comes from a video game.

title: #14. Personal Belief
text:
One personal belief I strongly hold is that consistent effort is more important than natural talent.

I think talent can give people an advantage at the beginning, but it is not enough to achieve something meaningful. In many cases, people improve because they keep practicing, make mistakes, and learn from them.

For example, when I started programming, I was not good at everything at first. I often felt confused when I solved problems or built small projects. But the more I practiced, the easier it became. This experience taught me that steady effort can turn a difficult skill into something more manageable.

I think the same idea applies to English, sports, and even work. So, I believe people should not give up too quickly just because they are not naturally talented. If they keep trying with the right attitude, they can make real progress over time.
